caption:
DeepGreen's filing names a Universal Docking Cradle. FERC's June letter said much of the underwater hardware lacked dimensions.

Checked August 21st, the Federal Register holds zero DeepGreen documents and seven for Cook Inlet hydrokinetic. FERC says comment comes after staff find a file complete.

This month Eastport, Maine voted unanimously for a 180 day moratorium on the same company's proposed underwater AI data center. It had already dropped from 51 megawatts to a maximum of 15.

February's filing asked for 1,650 acres of Cook Inlet seabed and up to four years of priority to study it. Its parent had formed in January.

The deck sets 1,650 acres against Maine's 400, the empty Federal Register row, and Curtis Thayer of the Alaska Energy Authority saying nobody called.

When the comment window opens on Cook Inlet, what would you want measured first?

#CookInlet #FERC #SubseaDataCenters

Anchorage Daily News, Bella Biondini, Underwater data center proposed for Alaska's Cook Inlet by East Coast company, 2026-08-19, https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/08/19/underwater-data-center-proposed-for-alaskas-cook-inlet-by-east-coast-company/

FERC, Northwest Branch, Division of Hydropower Licensing, the June 18th deficiency letter on the Cook Inlet application, not posted to a public page, quoted in the Anchorage Daily News report above

The Maine Monitor, Eastport adopts moratorium on underwater data center proposal, 2026-08-13, https://themainemonitor.org/eastport-adopts-moratorium-underwater-data-center-proposal/

The Quoddy Tides, Edward French, Proposed tidal project would power underwater AI data center, 2026-02-27, https://www.quoddytides.com/proposed-tidal-project-would-power-underwater-ai-data-center/

Every filing this page tracks, with the live deadlines beside it, sits at https://alaskaaihq.com

Anyone holding a document, a correction or local knowledge of these waters, add it below and it gets checked against the record.
aftercare: Post Tuesday through Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time, which is the strongest slot this page has.
Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of publishing, then pin it. Split it after the Quoddy Tides line if LinkedIn truncates at its comment ceiling.
Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. That window is where a carousel either gains reach or stalls.

Watch for anyone reading the zero result as proof the application does not exist. It proves no notice has published, which is the step that opens comment, and that correction should go out fast and plainly.
Watch for a commenter quoting the $400 million PowerLink figure as settled. AEA's own page says $142 million, both numbers are on slide 08, and neither one is settled.

Watch for a 94 percent claim about the Maine cut. The verified reductions are capacity, 51 megawatts to a maximum of 15, and turbines, about 170 down to 16 in a first phase. There is no verified area percentage.

Watch for readers in Nikiski and Kenai and from the tribes and Native corporations FERC said were not identified. Ask them what they would want measured, since that is the answer this post exists to collect.
Note saves and comments at 48 hours against the run ledger. Saves are the signal a keepable deck is built for.

editor_notes_for_email:
SITE SIGN-OFF: PASS, 83 pages, 18 checks.
GAS WATCH: PASS, read 2026-08-20, 16 days on record, no gaps, chart present, model misses by 6.82 percent.
SITE FIXES: mobile nav hit area grown from 28px to 36px in scripts/site_build.py, no layout shift.

CAPTION ROOM. Two candidates. The critic killed candidate A outright for reproducing the 2026-08-09 hook frame with the noun swapped, and for being the third count-first opening in six runs. The winner took one fix (a FERC finding attributed to the wrong object) and one accuracy correction (a Maine reduction dated to a month the claim does not carry). Its assigned close was a threshold test, which is a sufficiency test with a size variable and was already burned, so it was replaced.

SOURCING CAVEAT. The Federal Register zero result is a PRIMARY absence and it is only citable because the control query works: seven documents for 'Cook Inlet hydrokinetic' against zero for 'DeepGreen'. It proves no notice has PUBLISHED. It does not prove the application does not exist, and the aftercare list carries that correction first because it is the misreading most likely in the comments.
